tweet_summary: Video clip of Trump telling reporters he had 'nothing to do with' a Texas State Senate District 9 special election that a Democrat won in a district he carried by 17 points, claiming it was just a local race he knew nothing about.
why_note_decision: Trump's 'I had nothing to do with it / I'm not involved' is misleading: he publicly endorsed Republican Leigh Wambsganss on Truth Social, called her a 'MAGA Warrior,' and urged voters to 'KEEP TEXAS RED' the day before the election. Wambsganss then lost to Democrat Taylor Rehmet (~57-43). A note correcting the disavowal is warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note establishes that Trump DID involve himself in the race — specifically that he publicly endorsed the Republican candidate (Leigh Wambsganss) and urged people to vote for her shortly before the election — contradicting his on-camera claim of having 'nothing to do with it.' The note must name the endorsement (not merely say 'he was involved'). Bonus accuracy: the Democrat (Taylor Rehmet) won a district Trump carried by ~17 points. A note that only restates the election result without documenting Trump's endorsement FAILS to address the misleading claim.
reference_note: Contrary to Donald Trump’s claim that he had "nothing to do with" the Texas State Senate District 9 special election, he had endorsed and promoted the Republican candidate, Leigh Wambsganss, before her loss to Democrat Taylor Rehmet.    https://www.politico.com/news/2026/02/01/democrat-wins-a-reliably-republican-texas-state-senate-seat-stunning-gop-00759046

fact_check.notes: Trump endorsed Wambsganss on Truth Social ('true MAGA Warrior', 'KEEP TEXAS RED') and urged a vote for her the day before; she lost to Rehmet. His 'nothing to do with it' is a documented disavowal of his own endorsement.

importance.lens_rationale: 1.5M impressions; corrects a head-of-state misrepresenting his own electoral involvement — meaningful for democratic accountability and information integrity.
